newsitem.title: CANADA: Indonesia's appeal undiminished for gold explorers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's appeal undiminished for gold explorers.

text.p: Despite a pall cast by Bre-X Minerals Ltd, junior resource companies say their enthusiasm for projects in Indonesia remains undiminished.
Small companies at a Canadian mining conference said on Thursday they are proceeding with aggressive exploration in Indonesia with hopes of discovering another major gold deposit.

Bre-X started the scramble with its massive Busang gold discovery. But an ownership dispute there has lopped more than 20 percent off its share value in recent weeks and turned investors wary on the sector.

Despite the mood shift, exploration company executives said they are charging ahead while learning from what they described as Bre-X's main mistake -- not ensuring it had clear title to its property before before proving a big discovery.
Busang is estimated to contain 47 million ounces of gold and some analysts speculate it could have 100 million ounces.
"Indonesia really has tremendous potential. It's a great mining frontier that is just beginning," said Lou Clinton, chairman Omax Resources Ltd which has five projects underway in the Asian country.
He estimated that three-quarters of the discoveries in Indonesia were being made by junior companies, many of them from Canada and inspired by Bre-X.
Brian Fagan, editor of Asian World Stock Report, said he expected Indonesia to return to favor despite the current nervousness caused by Bre-X.

"The big question in Indonesia is, can it remain such a hot spot for exploration...given the difficulties Bre-X has been having," he said. His assessment was that "both financial markets and companies are willing to go one more round in Indonesia."
More than 130 Canadian companies are now working on Indonesia's main islands. They have raised an estimated C$500 million to C$750 million for their efforts, he said.
"The exploration potential in southeast Asia generally and Indonesia specifically is phenomenal," said Tony Climie, president of Mindoro Resources Ltd which has assembled properties in Indonesia.
Brett Resources Inc, which has three projects on the Indonesian island of Kalimantan where Bre-X's Busang is and one on Sumatra, said it is intent on acquiring more ground on Kalimantan.

Reflecting on Bre-X, executives said its experience showed the importance of securing a finalized contract of work from the Indonesian government before proving up a big discovery and the need for prominent Indonesian partners.

Bre-X was vulnerable to the ownership dispute because its rights to the ground were were apparently not secure when the potential of Busang became known and it did not have influential local partners, said Mike Andrews, director of gold operations for Meekatharra Minerals Ltd.
Bre-X has since formed an alliance with the son of Indonesian President Suharto and analysts have speculated that it its contract of work may soon win final approval.

Andrews said his company, which is working with Teck Corp, has lined up prominent Indonesian partners for its properties by awarding them a minority carried interest. "It's very helpful...in getting progress through the bureaucracy," he said.

Despite Bre-X's difficulties, exploration officials said Indonesia offered a good operating climate compared to many other developing countries. "Indonesia is a very good place to work...what you hear about Bre-X not withstanding," said Climie. "It's very easy to do business there."
